alignments.note: Verbless clause with an adjectival predicate: under rule 53 the whole supplied verbal frame *Let ... be had* rides with the predicate adjective, not with the subject noun *marriage*, discontinuously under rule 15. Rule 17 heads the unit on the meaning-bearing complement *honor* (the ASV renders τίμιος by the support phrase *had in honor*), not on the auxiliary *Let* or on *had*. Heading on *had* was the competing reading and is rejected because *had* is the empty support verb.
The ASV gives *marriage* no determiner, so the article has no English word to anchor: rule 23.
Subject noun, bare in the ASV.
ἐν rendered *among*; rule 36 keeps the English preposition on the Greek preposition.
Anarthrous substantival adjective taking its own English word; rule 26 splits it from the preposition.
Article realized by *the* under rule 19; the supplied *let* is not the article's but the predicate adjective's under rule 53.
Recoverable token pair with its article under rule 26.

Second verbless clause, analysed exactly as the first (rule 24): the adjectival predicate carries the supplied *let ... be* under rule 53, discontinuously under rule 15, headed on the adjective's own English word *undefiled*.
Postpositive γάρ realized by the clause-initial *for*; variant SBLGNT.HEB.13.4.v001 selected r00-base, which covers this token.
Coordinating conjunction between the two objects.
Future indicative with its English auxiliary; rule 9 heads the unit on the lexical verb *judge*.
The ASV writes a bare *God* with no determiner, so the article realizes nothing: rule 23.
Subject noun, split from its unrepresented article under rule 13.

review_notes: Every s### and t### id is partitioned exactly once; 16 source and 21 target tokens accounted for.

Both verbless clauses are analysed alike under rules 24 and 53: the supplied *Let ... be had* and *let ... be* ride with the predicate adjectives τίμιος and ἀμίαντος rather than with the subjects γάμος and κοίτη, against the ASV's word order, which rule 53 explicitly refuses as a test.
Heads reviewed separately: *honor* over *had* for τίμιος (rule 17's meaning-bearing complement), *judge* over *will* for κρινεῖ (rule 9).
Both articles before determinerless English nouns (ὁ γάμος, ὁ θεός) are their own unrepresented units under rules 13 and 23; ἡ κοίτη keeps its *the* under rule 19.
